title: regional-fallback-breadcrumbs-scratch
content:
Quick scratchpad: breadcrumbs and commands I ran while chasing the smart-routing / fallback incident that caused EU region 5xxs on 2026-03-09 -> 2026-03-10. Purpose: capture ad-hoc commands, error snippets, hypotheses, and next actions for handoff to SRE/infra.

Timeline (local times, UTC+0):
- 2026-03-09 23:58 UTC: alert from ops-monitoring: spike in 5xx for hosted-api in eu-west-1. Error rate ~12% for 10m.
- 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC: first on-call triage. Noted correlated latency increase in routing decisions.
- 2026-03-10 00:12 UTC: temporary config change rolled out (feature flag: routing.fallback_to_compatible=true) — ops said this should reduce hard failures by falling back to compatible quantized variants.
- 2026-03-10 00:20 UTC: 5xx rate jumped further to 28%.
- 2026-03-10 00:27 UTC: rollback of feature flag (set to false). Errors dropped to ~6% but still elevated.
- 2026-03-10 01:05 UTC: start deeper debug (commands below).

Commands and outputs (copied raw where useful):
- Check requests hitting routing-proxy in eu-west-1
  kubectl -n routing logs -l app=routing-proxy -c proxy | grep "route_decision" | tail -n 50
  -> sample lines: "route_decision id=rc-56a1 selector=latency_preferred fallback=compatible TRUE reason=variant_unavailable"

- Probe health endpoints of model-backends in eu-west-1
  for pod in $(kubectl -n models get pods -l region=eu-west-1 -o name); do kubectl -n models exec $pod -- curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health || echo "HEALTH FAIL $pod"; done
  -> multiple pods returned 200, but 3/8 returned slow responses (~800ms). No outright 500s.

- Envoy upstream check (on routing-proxy pod)
  curl -sS localhost:9001/clusters | grep -A2 "models_eu_west" 
  -> outlier detection: 2 hosts marked unhealthy, ejection percentage increased from 5% -> 30% around 00:10 UTC

- Check model variant availability index (internal service)
  curl -sS https://model-catalog.internal/api/v1/variants?model=redwood-xl | jq .
  -> returned that "redwood-xl-8q" was present in eu-west-1 but "redwood-xl-16q" was not; fallback policy should pick 8q if compatible flag enabled. But routing logs show 'variant_unavailable' even though catalog says available.

- Look at routing decision logs (sample)
  2026-03-10T00:09:57Z route_id=abc123 user=svc-batch model=redwood-xl requested_variant=16q selected_variant=null reason=variant_missing fallback_allowed=true fallback_variant=null
  -> interesting: fallback_allowed=true but fallback_variant=null; that explains immediate 5xx.

- Investigated cache (KV cache for variant lookups)
  redis-cli -h redis-eu.stats GET variant:redwood-xl:16q
  -> returned nil for many keys; TTL show recent invalidations at 00:07 UTC.

- Looked at recent infra changes (from linked PRs)
  git log --since='2026-03-09' --pretty=oneline infra/routing | head
  -> PR #834 modified fallback resolution code to prefer region-local variants and introduced new cache invalidation when model manifests refresh.

Error snippets observed in service logs:
- "no healthy upstream: models_eu_west (503)"
- "fallback_resolution_failed: no compatible variant found"
- "route_decision error: inconsistent-catalog-cache"
- HTTP traces: 502 from routing-proxy -> model-backend timeout after 2s

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cache-invalidation race introduced in PR #834: during manifest refresh the variant resolution cache gets cleared and fallback-resolver tries to read it before it rebuilds -> leads to fallback_allowed true but no fallback_variant available.
2) Health-check sensitivity + outlier ejection was too aggressive when combined with the new "prefer-local" heuristic; ejected hosts reduced capacity below threshold causing routing to hit fallback path more often.
3) A recent change to the fallback policy changed ordering: prefer_compatible=true but compatibility check calls an internal comparator that throws for some quantized variants (edge case), causing resolver to abort.
4) Network blips between routing-proxy and catalog service caused transient lookups to return empty and triggered missing fallback_variant condition.

Reproduction attempts / experiments run:
- Force variant catalog to be immutable (disabled refresh) on one staging instance and replay traffic: no 5xxs observed. Suggests cache refresh logic is suspect.
- Manually set variant entries in redis for the negative cases and re-ran test traffic: routes repaired and success rate improved.
- Toggled env var ROUTER_FALLBACK_GRACE_MS to 500ms -> decreased immediate 5xxs but increased tail latency.
- Scaled up model-backends in eu-west-1 by +30% (autoscaler override): reduced 5xx by ~8% but did not fully resolve.

Immediate mitigations applied (notes):
- Rolled back PR #834 in infra routing (2026-03-10 00:30 UTC) — partial improvement.
- Increased healthcheck window to avoid aggressive ejection (00:42 UTC) -> fewer ejections, capacity stabilized.
- Hotpatched routing-proxy to treat empty fallback_variant as 'try remote region' instead of immediate 5xx (temporary guard).

Observations after mitigations:
- Error rate fell to ~2-3% and stabilized. Tail latency increased slightly for cross-region fallbacks.
- A minority of requests still hit fallback errors; traces show catalog reads failed with 503 for a small subset (likely transient network issue to catalog nodes in eu-west region).

Open action items / follow-ups:
- [High] Postmortem write-up (owner: Aisha) with timeline, RCA, and long-term fixes. Target: 2026-03-12 EOD.
- [High] Rework cache-refresh logic: ensure atomic swap semantics so resolver never sees an empty state. (Owner: Tom). Link: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/840
- [Medium] Add synthetic tests that exercise manifest refresh under load to catch race conditions. (Owner: SRE)
- [Medium] Add stricter observability around fallback_resolution path: instrument when fallback_allowed=true and fallback_variant==null (new metric). (Owner: Leah)
- [Low] Re-evaluate outlier ejection thresholds for eu-west workload patterns.
- [Low] Update runbook: when toggling fallback flags, do staged canary with traffic mirroring first.

Notes for handoff:
- Key logs: routing-proxy logs around 2026-03-10T00:06:00Z to 00:18:00Z (request ids prefixed rc- or route-). Search for 'fallback_variant=null'.
- Catalog service logs: index refresh events at 00:06-00:08 UTC; correlate with redis key expirations.
- PR to inspect: infra/routing #834 (rollback) and pending fix #840.

Misc mental notes / raw ideas (untested):
- Could implement a tiny in-memory generation counter for catalog snapshots; publish snapshot_id and have resolver wait for first snapshot if cache empty for < X ms before declaring missing.
- Consider a "graceful_missing" mode where routing will attempt remote region lookup synchronously instead of returning 5xx immediately when local fallback_variant is missing.

Last commands I ran before leaving:
- kubectl -n routing exec -it $(kubectl -n routing get pods -l app=routing-proxy -o name | head -n1) -- tail -n 200 /var/log/routing-proxy.log | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/routing-tail-200.txt
- redis-cli -h redis-eu.monitor INFO keyspace > /tmp/redis-keyspace-eu.txt

If you're picking this up: start by grepping for 'fallback_variant=null' across routing-proxy logs and then check catalog refresh events. Ping me on Slack (aisha) if you need the session keys / copies of the command outputs I saved on my laptop.

End of scratchpad.
